environment: Humpback whale super-highway peaks off the Queensland coast as spring migration draws record crowds to the Gold and Sunshine Coasts
Great Barrier Reef coral colonies showing strong signs of recovery as marine scientists prepare for the annual spawning season
science: Aussie researchers push solar cell efficiency to new highs with next generation perovskite technology
sports: NRL finals fever grips the nation as the first week of September finals kicks off with Queensland teams in the mix
stories.overview: Queensland's coastline turns into a whale watching wonderland as humpback numbers keep climbing year on year

segments.title: The Open
segments.script: G'day and welcome to ParkSyde Bright Side, I'm Alex Mercer, and mate, it is a ripper of a Saturday to be alive in Queensland. Whales are putting on a show, the reef's looking healthier, and footy finals are finally here. Grab your cuppa, settle in, we've got a beauty of a bulletin for you. I'm Jamie, and honestly Alex, I don't know where to start, this is one of those weeks where every pillar's got a win in it. Environment, science, sport, even the weather's playing nice for a change. It's giving me a serious case of the warm fuzzies. Warm fuzzies and warm weather, Jamie, don't jinx it. Let's get into it, starting with something splashing about off our own coastline that's honestly one of nature's best shows.

segments.title: Green Desk
segments.script: So Alex, it's peak humpback whale season right now and the numbers are just phenomenal. Boats out of the Gold Coast and Hervey Bay are reporting whales basically everywhere you look, breaching, tail slapping, the whole lot. Yeah I heard a bloke on the radio say he counted a dozen breaches in twenty minutes off Burleigh, which is a pretty good strike rate for a Saturday arvo. These fellas are cruising up from Antarctica to have their calves in our warmer waters, then heading home again, it's an epic road trip really. And here's the good news bit, populations have been steadily climbing for years now after being hunted almost to nothing last century. Meanwhile marine biologists are chuffed with how the Great Barrier Reef is looking heading into spawning season, coral cover is holding up better than a lot of people expected.

segments.title: Science & Tomorrow
segments.script: Right, from whales to watts, Jamie, because Aussie scientists are quietly having a crack at solving the whole energy puzzle. Researchers here have been squeezing more and more efficiency out of these perovskite solar cells, which sounds like a Harry Potter spell but is actually next level solar tech. It's genuinely exciting stuff, these cells are cheaper to make than traditional silicon panels and can be layered up to capture more sunlight, more efficiently. If the lab results keep translating to the real world, we could be looking at solar power that's even more affordable for everyday households. Love that for us, because between the reef bouncing back and the sun literally powering our future, Queensland's punching well above its weight this week. Right, speaking of sunshine, let's see what it's actually doing outside, over to Sam.

segments.title: Weather
segments.script: Cheers Alex, and look, it's shaping up as a cracking spring Saturday across the south east. Brisbane's set for clear skies and a top around twenty three, with light south easterly winds keeping things pleasant rather than parky. The Gold and Sunshine Coasts are looking similarly glorious, mid twenties, plenty of sun, an absolute cracker for those whale watching boats Jamie was just talking about. Further inland toward Toowoomba it'll be a touch cooler overnight but still a fine and dry day, and we're not expecting any rain to speak of anywhere in the south east this weekend. Sunday's tracking much the same, so if you've got outdoor plans, footy, fishing, or just a snag on the barbie, you are in luck. Back to you Alex.
